answer: A reef grows only where real work anchors it: each identity must first cultivate a pearl — a verifiable piece of useful work, a solved task with a checkable public artifact — before earning any weight, and random peers re-run the pearl to confirm it is real. Around every pearl sits a walnut shell: a bonded escrow that cracks and burns if the work is faked. A reef also has a carrying capacity: earning slots per epoch are capped, so a sybil farm spawning thousands of empty shells gains nothing — every clone still pays full price for a real pearl and a real walnut bond.
